problem_text:
A logistics manager must assemble a shipment of specialized components to maximize total utility score while staying within the cargo plane's maximum payload allowance.

The components available are:
* Component A: mass 24 units, utility 108 credits
* Component B: mass 13 units, utility 161 credits
* Component C: mass 34 units, utility 227 credits
* Component D: mass 42 units, utility 203 credits
* Component E: mass 26 units, utility 28 credits
* Component F: mass 10 units, utility 235 credits
* Component G: mass 5 units, utility 157 credits
* Component H: mass 41 units, utility 89 credits
* Component I: mass 34 units, utility 106 credits
* Component J: mass 39 units, utility 260 credits
* Component K: mass 23 units, utility 89 credits
* Component L: mass 38 units, utility 86 credits
* Component M: mass 37 units, utility 229 credits
* Component N: mass 17 units, utility 118 credits
* Component O: mass 8 units, utility 90 credits
* Component P: mass 9 units, utility 236 credits
* Component Q: mass 35 units, utility 226 credits
* Component R: mass 12 units, utility 29 credits
* Component S: mass 20 units, utility 250 credits

Furthermore, due to compatibility restrictions, exactly one of Component A and Component B must be included in the final shipment.

If Component C is selected, it necessitates special handling equipment that reduces the effective payload capacity of the aircraft by 10 units.
The aircraft can transport a maximum of 326 units. The manager must determine the optimal selection of components.
